Alexandria by the numbers

Where is Alexandria, VA, and how is the city laid out?

Alexandria is an independent city on the west bank of the Potomac River, about 15.35 square miles in size, with Washington, D.C. to the northeast, Arlington County to the north and northwest, and Fairfax County to the south (Wikipedia). Elevation runs from sea level to 287 feet.

Because it is an independent city, Alexandria bills its own real estate tax and has no county government above it. The city's main neighborhoods give a sense of the housing mix:

  • Old Town, the historic core near the river
  • Del Ray and Potomac, the former town of Potomac
  • Carlyle and Eisenhower East
  • Rosemont, West End, Potomac Yard and Arlandria

The city had 159,467 residents in the 2020 census and a 2025 estimate of 160,662. Median household income was $124,593 in the 2024 American Community Survey estimate.

What is the history that still shapes Alexandria property?

Alexandria was founded in 1749, became a town in 1779 and was ceded to the District of Columbia in 1801 before returning to Virginia in 1847. It was chartered as a city in 1852 and became independent in 1870, and annexations in 1915, 1930 and 1952 expanded its borders.

The Old Town historic district, created in 1946, was the third in the country. That history is why many Alexandria houses are regulated by a review board, as the next section explains.

Do historic district rules affect selling an Alexandria house?

They can, because exterior work in a local historic district needs approval from the Board of Architectural Review. The city regulates two local districts, Old and Historic Alexandria and Parker-Gray, plus buildings designated as One Hundred-Year-Old Buildings (Historic Preservation page).

  • A Certificate of Appropriateness is required for new construction and exterior alterations visible from a public right of way.
  • A Permit to Demolish is needed to demolish or encapsulate more than 25 square feet of material, whether or not it is visible.
  • Interior work does not need board approval.
  • Staff can approve some projects administratively, usually in under five business days.

The city offers a Historic Preservation map viewer to check whether an address is in a district. Preservation staff can be reached at 703.746.3833 or Preservation@alexandriava.gov.

What drives the Alexandria economy?

The federal government is the largest force in the city's economy. The biggest employers named are the Pentagon's Mark Center, with about 8,000 workers, and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, with about 6,000. Tourism passed $1 billion in visitor revenue in 2024.

Metro's Blue and Yellow lines serve the city, with stations at King Street-Old Town, Braddock Road, Eisenhower Avenue and Van Dorn Street, and a Potomac Yard station that opened in 2023. The city runs its own DASH bus system, and Interstates 95, 495 and 395 and US 1 pass through it.

Alexandria City Public Schools operates 12 elementary schools, two pre-K through 8 schools, two middle schools and Alexandria City High School, which has two campuses.

What did the 2026 Alexandria assessment show?

Alexandria's total tax base rose 3.41 percent for 2026, the fifteenth straight year of net increase, and residential assessments rose 4.40 percent overall. The figures come from the Office of Real Estate Assessments notice insert (2026 key dates insert).

Category2026 figure
Average existing residential value$757,706 (up 3.81%)
Average single-family home$1,045,750 (up 4.44%)
Average condo$460,185 (up 2.81%)
Commercial overallup 1.91%
Officedown 3.40%

Of residential properties, 63 percent went up, 8 percent went down and 29 percent stayed the same. Only sales completed before January 1, 2026 counted toward the assessed values.

What are the 2026 Alexandria tax dates in order?

The city's 2026 key-dates insert lists the full calendar, and the notice itself is not a bill. The calendar below uses the dates printed on that insert.

  • February 25: assessment notices mailed.
  • March 16: deadline to request an administrative review. The city says no exceptions will be made to appeal deadlines.
  • April 15: deadline for elderly and disabled tax relief applications.
  • April 29: City Council adopts the FY 2027 budget and sets the tax rate.
  • June 1: deadline to appeal to the Board of Equalization.
  • June 15: first-half payment due, even if a review or appeal is pending.
  • Early October: second-half bills mailed.
  • November 16: second-half payment due. November 15 falls on a Sunday in 2026.

To start a review, email realestate@alexandriava.gov or call 703.746.4168.

Does Alexandria offer tax relief for older or disabled owners?

Yes. Alexandria runs a real estate tax relief and deferral program for owners who are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. Completed applications or annual certifications are due to the Department of Finance by April 15 each year (program page).

  • Household net assets may not exceed $430,000, excluding the home, up to one acre of land and the related mortgage.
  • Household gross income counts the applicant, a spouse and other owners living in the home.
  • Late applications may be accepted until April 15 of the next year for good cause, such as a hospitalization or first-time filing.
  • Deferred taxes are repaid with interest when the property is conveyed or the owner dies. Relieved taxes are not repaid.

The city's phone line is 703.746.4800, option 6, and the email is taxrelief@alexandriava.gov. The page we opened did not show the income limit, so ask the office for the current figure.

The deferral matters in a sale. If you deferred tax, the repayment falls due when the house is conveyed, so ask for the balance at the start.

Does the Potomac flood Old Town properties?

Parts of Old Town flood during storm surge and some low inlets flood from the tide alone. A city analysis of Potomac gauge data from 2004 to 2021 found the river above Action Stage about 112 days a year and above Flood Stage about 16 days a year (city flood frequency memo).

EventRiver level
Hurricane Isabel, September 20038.66 feet, highest on record
Great Potomac Flood, March 19367.40 feet
October 2021 nor'easter5.99 feet
Tropical Storm Ernesto, September 20065.54 feet

The memo names King Street at Strand and Union, and Union Street from Prince to Thompsons Alley, among the areas that flooded in 2021. Anyone selling near the waterfront should expect buyers to ask about flood insurance and past water in the basement or garage.

What does a deed transfer cost in Alexandria?

Virginia's state recordation tax on a deed is 25 cents per $100, applied to the greater of the price or the most recent assessment (Va. Code 58.1-801). A separate grantor's tax is 50 cents per $500 (58.1-802), and it excludes the value of liens that stay on the property.

The title company will prepare a settlement statement that shows these charges and the property tax payoff. Local and other recording charges are not covered here, so ask the title company.

How do sellers with Alexandria tax due usually proceed?

An Alexandria seller with unpaid tax can sell, and the title company pays the balance from proceeds. Ask the Treasury Division for a payoff that includes any penalty, and confirm whether the half-year bill already issued has been paid.

This page is general information. The city offices and a Virginia attorney can confirm figures for your parcel.

More questions about Alexandria, VA Property Tax Guide

When is Alexandria property tax due in 2026?

The first half is due June 15, 2026, and the second half is due November 16, 2026, because November 15 falls on a Sunday. The city says the first payment is due even if a review or appeal is pending.

How do I appeal my Alexandria assessment?

Request an administrative review by March 16, 2026, then appeal to the Board of Equalization by June 1 if you still disagree. Email realestate@alexandriava.gov or call 703.746.4168.

Does Alexandria have tax relief for seniors?

Yes. Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, can apply by April 15 each year, with household net assets capped at $430,000 excluding the home and up to one acre. Call 703.746.4800, option 6.

Do I need approval to change the outside of a house in Old Town?

Usually yes, if the house is in a local historic district and the work is visible from a public right of way. The Board of Architectural Review issues a Certificate of Appropriateness, and interior work does not need it.

How much did Alexandria assessments rise in 2026?

The total tax base rose 3.41 percent and residential assessments rose 4.40 percent. The average single-family home was valued at $1,045,750 and the average condo at $460,185.

Hampton by the numbers

Where is Hampton, Virginia, and how big is it?

Hampton is an independent city on the Virginia Peninsula in the Hampton Roads region, so it is not inside any county and bills its own real estate tax. The 2020 census counted 137,148 residents, which made it the seventh most populous city in Virginia, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 137,315.

The city covers 136.27 square miles, but only 51.46 of them are land because about 62 percent of the area is water. Elevation averages about 10 feet, which is why flooding comes up in most Hampton house conversations.

It borders Newport News and Poquoson, and Hampton Roads Transit runs the local buses.

ItemFigure from the sources
Type of localityIndependent city
2020 census population137,148
Total area136.27 square miles (51.46 land)
Housing units, 202062,444, with 7.7% vacant
Households, 202057,612
Median age, 202037.2 years
Real estate tax rate$1.14 per $100 of assessed value

What is the history of Hampton?

Hampton claims to be the oldest continuously occupied English settlement in the United States, with the colonists establishing a town and what is now St. John's Episcopal Church in 1610. It became a town in 1705, a city in 1849 and an independent city in 1908.

On July 1, 1952, the city of Hampton, the town of Phoebus and Elizabeth City County merged into one independent city after voters approved. That merger is why older Hampton records may mention Elizabeth City County.

Fort Monroe, at Old Point Comfort, was decommissioned as an army base on September 15, 2011 and named a national monument that November. Hampton University was founded after the Civil War across the Hampton River from the fort.

What jobs and institutions shape Hampton?

The federal presence is large. Langley Air Force Base, the nation's first military installation dedicated to air power, is in Hampton, and so is NASA's Langley Research Center.

Other anchors are Hampton University, Virginia Peninsula Community College, the Virginia Air and Space Science Center and the Hampton Coliseum. Wikipedia also notes a NASCAR short track and a long Navy and Air Force family presence.

Military assignments mean some Hampton owners move on short notice. A deployed or transferred owner who needs to sell may not have time for repairs and showings.

Which neighborhoods make up Hampton?

The city's neighborhoods include Aberdeen Gardens, Buckroe Beach, Farmington, Fox Hill, Hampton Woods, Northampton, Newmarket, Phoebus, the Victoria Boulevard Historic District and Wythe, which includes the Olde Wythe Historic District.

Historic district status can limit exterior changes, so a seller in Olde Wythe or Phoebus should ask city planning staff what applies to the address. We did not open an official page on district rules, so we do not summarize them here.

  • Waterfront areas such as Buckroe Beach and Fox Hill raise flood and insurance questions.
  • Old Hampton and Phoebus date to the colonial and 19th-century town centers.
  • Phoebus was its own town until the 1952 merger.

What does the climate mean for a Hampton house?

Hampton has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild winters. Wikipedia gives a mean annual temperature of 60.2 degrees Fahrenheit, about 47 inches of rain and about 6 inches of snow a year.

The highest temperature on record was 105.1 degrees on August 1, 1980. For a house, that means attention to roofs, gutters, crawl space moisture and air conditioning age. We did not open an official Hampton flood-zone page, so ask the city and your insurer about the address.

How do roads and transit affect Hampton homes?

Interstate 64 and Interstate 664 meet near the Hampton Coliseum. The Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel is on I-64 near downtown Hampton, and the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel is on I-664 nearby in Newport News.

U.S. routes 17, 60 and 258 and State Routes 134 and 143 also serve the city. The Hampton Transit Center at West Pembroke Avenue and King Street is a hub for Hampton Roads Transit buses, and Amtrak runs from the Newport News station.

Which schools serve Hampton?

Hampton City Public Schools runs four high schools, Kecoughtan, Bethel, Phoebus and Hampton, along with elementary, middle and specialty schools.

Zone boundaries depend on the address, so check with the division before quoting a school to a buyer.

Who bills and who assesses real estate tax in Hampton?

The City Assessor sets the value, and the Treasurer bills and collects. The assessor's office is at One Franklin Street, Suite 602, phone 757-727-8311. The Treasurer is at One Franklin Street, Suite 100, phone 757-727-6374.

The city says all real estate is appraised each year and assessed at 100 percent of market value, and that the real estate tax rate is $1.14 per $100 of assessed value. The tax year runs from July 1 to June 30.

The Treasurer also takes payments online, by mail, in the drop box at One Franklin Street, and by phone at (877) 277-6341.

When are Hampton real estate taxes due?

Hampton real estate tax is due in two equal installments, on June 5 and December 5. A 10 percent penalty applies if the bill is not paid by the due date, and interest at 10 percent a year accrues on unpaid balances starting July 1.

  • The Treasurer's page says bills are mailed the last Friday in April and the last Friday in October.
  • A separate real estate page says first-half bills mail about November 1 for December 5, and second-half bills about May 1 for June 5.
  • Because the two pages differ on mailing dates, rely on the due dates and the date printed on your bill.

The page also says taxes may be paid in full when the first installment is due.

How do you appeal a Hampton assessment?

There are three levels. An Office Review Application must be filed within 30 days of the assessment notice date, and the city suggests calling an appraiser first.

A Board of Review application is due within 60 days of the notice date, and you do not need an Office Review first. The board has five members who are Hampton property owners, hears cases mostly in May and June at the Ruppert Sargent Building and may raise, lower or affirm a value.

You can also petition the Circuit Court directly without either earlier step. For a supplemental assessment on new construction or an addition, the appeal window is 30 days from the notice.

What happens to unpaid tax when a Hampton house sells?

Virginia's Code puts the real estate tax lien ahead of every other lien, and the closing agent pays the Treasurer from the sale proceeds. The statute's definition of taxes includes penalties and interest, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure good through the closing date.

What do sellers in Hampton usually face?

Owners here handle inherited houses, rental properties, older houses that need updates, and military moves. With 62,444 housing units and a 7.7 percent vacancy rate in 2020, there is steady turnover. We buy Hampton houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid real estate tax from your proceeds.

The city's real estate page lists $1.14 per $100 of assessed value, with property assessed at 100 percent of market value.

30 days from the notice date for an Office Review and 60 days for the Board of Review. You can petition the Circuit Court without either.

Who do I call about Hampton assessments?

The Assessor of Real Estate at 757-727-8311. For payments and balances call the Treasurer at 757-727-6374.

Can I sell a Hampton house with unpaid tax?

Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff from the Treasurer first.

Chesapeake by the numbers

Where is Chesapeake, Virginia, and how big is it?

Chesapeake is an independent city in the Hampton Roads area of southeastern Virginia. It borders Portsmouth and Norfolk to the north, Virginia Beach to the east, Suffolk to the west, and North Carolina's Currituck and Camden counties to the south.

The 2020 census counted 249,422 residents, making it the second most populous city in Virginia. By land area it is the second largest city in the state, with about 338.5 square miles of land and 12.4 square miles of water. Elevation is only 16 feet.

The modern city dates to 1963, when South Norfolk merged with what remained of Norfolk County, approved by referendum and authorized by the General Assembly. The Battle of Great Bridge was fought here on December 9, 1775.

What are Chesapeake's six boroughs and waterways?

The city is divided into six boroughs: South Norfolk, Butts Road, Deep Creek, Pleasant Grove, Western Branch and Washington. A house in each borough can feel very different, from dense older streets to large rural lots.

Water shapes the whole city. The northeastern part of the Great Dismal Swamp lies in Chesapeake, and the Great Dismal Swamp National Wildlife Refuge covers a large piece of it. The Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway passes through, along with the Western and Southern Branches of the Elizabeth River and the Dismal Swamp Canal, which runs parallel to U.S. Highway 17.

With an average elevation of 16 feet, much of the city sits low, so ask the city for the flood zone of your parcel before you list, particularly if the lot is near water.

What does the climate mean for a Chesapeake house?

Chesapeake has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. Annual precipitation averages about 48.4 inches, and mean daily highs run from roughly 49.7 degrees in January to 88.7 in July.

Humidity matters for houses. Crawl space moisture, attic ventilation and air conditioning load are typical items a buyer's inspector will raise, and a house with deferred upkeep can show those problems quickly.

Who employs people in Chesapeake and how do roads connect the city?

The largest employers are the public schools (6,248), the City of Chesapeake (3,927), Chesapeake Regional Medical Center (2,038), Walmart (1,783) and Sentara Healthcare (1,478). Dollar Tree has its international headquarters here, and the Navy runs Northwest Annex and NALF Fentress.

  • Interstates: I-64 (part of the Hampton Roads Beltway), I-464 and I-664.
  • U.S. highways: 13, 17, 58 and 460.
  • Tolls: the Chesapeake Expressway on State Route 168, Veterans Bridge and Jordan Bridge.
  • Five movable bridges, which open an estimated 30,000 times a year.

Norfolk International Airport serves the city, and five railroads, including CSX and Norfolk Southern, run through it. A bridge opening can slow a commute, which is a detail buyers ask about.

When are Chesapeake real estate taxes due?

Chesapeake bills real estate tax in four quarterly payments, which is different from the two payment schedule most Virginia localities use. The Treasurer's due dates page lists the dates below, and says a date that falls on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

PaymentDue date
1st quarterSeptember 30
2nd quarterDecember 31
3rd quarterMarch 31
4th quarterJune 5
Stormwater, 1st halfJune 5
Stormwater, 2nd halfDecember 31
Tax relief filingBy May 15

The page says penalty and interest are applied as required by state and city code if a payment is not postmarked or received by the deadline, and it gives no percentages. The ceilings in Code of Virginia 58.1-3916 are 10 percent for the property tax penalty and 10 percent a year for interest, so ask the Treasurer what the city actually charges.

What is the Chesapeake tax rate and stormwater fee?

The city lists a real estate tax rate of $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026 to 2027, which includes $0.01 for mosquito control. The stormwater fee for a single residence is $136.20 a year, paid in two installments of $68.10.

Under City Code Section 26-372, the stormwater fee is payable by the owner of the billed parcel. That matters for a sale, because a bill that is unpaid when you list may be there when you close.

The Treasurer's office can be emailed at paytax@cityofchesapeake.net, and the city main line is 757-382-2489. The address is 306 Cedar Road, Chesapeake, VA 23322.

How does the Chesapeake Real Estate Assessor set and change values?

Chesapeake values property as of January 1, and new values take effect July 1. Owners whose value changed are mailed a notice, and for the current cycle those notices go out on or before March 1, 2027.

New construction, additions and demolitions are picked up through supplemental bills, with valuation changes captured on October 1, January 1, April 1 and July 1. A teardown or an addition done before listing can therefore change the bill during the year.

The Assessor's office is at 306 Cedar Road, 4th Floor, with phone 757-382-6235 and email assessor@cityofchesapeake.net. A free property search is available at chesapeake.civ.quest, while the city's paid tax information subscription costs $1,100 a year or $100 a month.

How can you appeal a Chesapeake assessment?

Chesapeake gives owners three routes, and you can use more than one. You may contact the Assessor to schedule a property review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition the Circuit Court.

  • The Board application must show the property is valued above fair market value, or that the assessment is not applied uniformly, or does not follow accepted appraisal standards or Virginia law.
  • The city posts an Appeal Process guide, instructions for filing, and an application as PDFs.
  • The page says time limits apply but does not state them, so ask the Assessor's office before you plan.

For owners over 65 or disabled, the city runs tax relief through the Commissioner of the Revenue at 757-382-6455, option 4. Applications run from January 1 through May 15, and the city listed relief of 100 percent for household income up to $25,000 in fiscal year 2025. Check the current limits, because they are listed by year.

What should Chesapeake sellers watch for at closing?

Chesapeake sellers should confirm four things: the current quarter's real estate tax, the stormwater fee, any land use enrollment and the recordation costs. The city's own page notes that Virginia does not allow title transfer when delinquent taxes are paid through a tax lien sale, so back taxes can complicate a sale if they are left too long.

If the land is in the use value program, the minimums are 5 acres for agricultural, horticultural and open space land and 20 acres for forest land. A change in use or a rezoning at the owner's request can trigger rollback taxes covering the current year and the five most recent complete tax years, plus simple interest.

Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under 58.1-802. Cash Home Buyers can buy a Chesapeake house as is, including one with overdue tax, and the Treasurer's payoff can come out of the proceeds.

More questions about Chesapeake, VA Property Tax Guide

When are Chesapeake real estate taxes due?

In four quarterly payments: September 30, December 31, March 31 and June 5. A date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

What is the Chesapeake real estate tax rate?

The city lists $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026 to 2027, which includes $0.01 for mosquito control.

How do I appeal a Chesapeake assessment?

Contact the Real Estate Assessor at 757-382-6235 for a property review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition the Circuit Court. You can use more than one route.

What is the Chesapeake stormwater fee?

For a single residence the city lists $136.20 a year, due in two installments of $68.10 on June 5 and December 31. The owner of the billed parcel pays it.

Can I sell my Chesapeake house with unpaid taxes?

Yes, the balance is normally settled from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that matches your closing date.

Charlottesville by the numbers

What kind of place is Charlottesville, Virginia?

Charlottesville is an independent city in central Virginia, on the Rivanna River, with Albemarle County all around it. It is the county seat of Albemarle, but the city and county are separate governments, and that matters for a property tax bill because only the city bills city addresses.

The city covers 10.27 square miles and had 46,553 residents in the 2020 census. It is about 99 miles from Washington, D.C., and 72 miles from Richmond, at an elevation of 594 feet.

Charlottesville was founded in 1762 and named for Queen Charlotte. Its historic center is Court Square, and its Downtown Mall is described as one of the longest outdoor pedestrian malls in the country.

How does the University of Virginia shape Charlottesville housing?

The University of Virginia is the largest force in the local housing picture. Its main grounds are on the city's west side, though most of the campus sits legally in Albemarle County, and more than 20,000 students come to the area in the academic year.

The biggest employers, each with over 1,000 workers, are UVA and its hospital, the UVA Health Services Foundation, the City of Charlottesville and the city school board. Crutchfield, Emerson Automation Solutions, PepsiCo and S&P Global are also listed. About 82 percent of people employed in the city commute in from elsewhere, so many workers hold a Charlottesville job and a house in another locality.

The text we read names Ridge Street, Fifeville, Tenth and Page, and Rose Hill as long-standing neighborhoods. Sellers in older streets near the university often own homes with age-related repair needs.

What is the weather like, and what does it mean for a Charlottesville house?

Charlottesville has a humid subtropical climate with four seasons. January averages 36.2 degrees Fahrenheit and July averages 77.6, and the city gets about 17 inches of snow in an average year.

That mix puts steady wear on roofs, gutters, older windows and heating systems. Record extremes run from minus 10 degrees in January 1994 to 107 in September 1954, so a house here can see both deep freezes and hot summers. A buyer's inspector will usually look hard at the roof and the heating equipment.

Which roads and trains reach Charlottesville?

Interstate 64 and U.S. Route 29 are the main highways. Charlottesville Union Station is served by Amtrak's Cardinal, Crescent and Northeast Regional routes, and the Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport serves the area.

Local transit includes Charlottesville Area Transit, JAUNT paratransit and University Transit Service. Homes with easy access to those routes and to downtown tend to draw more attention from buyers who commute without a car.

When are Charlottesville real estate taxes due and how much is the rate?

Charlottesville real estate tax is due in two equal installments, on June 5 and December 5, and the city lists a rate of $0.99 per $100 of assessed value. City Council sets the rate in the spring. If a deadline falls on a weekend, it moves to the following Monday.

ItemCity of Charlottesville
Due datesJune 5 and December 5
Rate$0.99 per $100 of assessed value
Late penalty10 percent of the tax due, the day after the deadline
Interest10 percent a year, accruing monthly
Treasurer phone434-970-3146
Mailing addressP.O. Box 2854, Charlottesville, VA 22902

A payment plan does not stop penalties and interest, according to the city. If the tax goes unpaid, the city lists bank account liens, rent liens and wage garnishments as collection methods, and says properties with three or more years of unpaid tax are subject to judicial sale. To ask for a penalty waiver, the city asks you to read its Late Payment Penalty Policy and write to the Treasurer with supporting documents.

How does the City Assessor value Charlottesville property?

The City Assessor values every parcel each year, as of January 1, and mails change of assessment notices at the end of January. Under city code, all real estate is assessed annually.

Most homes are valued by comparing recent sales of similar houses in the same neighborhood. The city says auctions, bank foreclosures, condemnations and transfers between family members generally do not count as arm's-length sales. That is useful to know if your house sold recently under unusual terms.

  • Office: 102 5th Street NE, Charlottesville, VA 22902, by appointment, phone 434-970-3136.
  • Mail: P.O. Box 911, Charlottesville, VA 22902.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 605 E Main Street, Room A-130, phone 434-970-3160.

Where can you look up Charlottesville property records?

The City Assessor keeps a history file for every parcel, with ownership, deed and plat references, ownership history and details of improvements. The city also publishes assessment neighborhood maps, land books and GIS data, and its GIS Viewer gives access to real estate records online. A public computer is available at the Assessor's office for the same purpose.

  • Assessment neighborhood maps and land books, posted on the city's assessor pages.
  • An Income and Expense form for income-producing property.
  • An Assessment Appeal Application form, which you can also request by phone.

Before you list, compare your record against the house itself. The city accepts factual discrepancies such as square footage, acreage or the condition of improvements as grounds for appeal, and a corrected record can lower the bill you pass to the next owner. If an agent files for you, include a Letter of Authorization.

How do you appeal a Charlottesville assessment?

Appeal in three steps: the assessor, the Board of Equalization, then Circuit Court. A high tax bill or a large jump in value is not enough by itself. The city accepts factual errors in the property record, uneven values within a neighborhood, and disagreements over fair market value.

  1. Call the appraiser at 434-970-3136 with your owner name, address or nine digit parcel ID. Many questions end here.
  2. File an Assessment Appeal Application with your reasoning and evidence. The appraiser may inspect the property and will mail a decision, which the city says comes within 30 days.
  3. Ask for a Board of Equalization review within 30 days of the decision letter. The board is an independent citizen panel appointed by the Circuit Court judge, and it mails its decision within 30 days after the hearing.
  4. As a last step, appeal to Circuit Court. You carry the burden of proof and pay court costs.

The city pages we opened do not give a filing deadline for the first application, so call the assessor's office to confirm it. Virginia law, in 58.1-3379, presumes the assessor's value is correct and requires the owner to rebut it with evidence.

What should Charlottesville sellers with unpaid tax know?

The main point is that the Treasurer's balance includes penalty and interest, so the payoff changes month to month. Ask the Treasurer at 434-970-3146 for a figure that matches your closing date.

The Commissioner of the Revenue lists tax relief programs for the elderly and disabled, a homeowner assistance program and an exemption for disabled veterans and surviving spouses. The page carries a note that the real estate relief program has ended, so confirm what is currently open before you count on it.

At closing, Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value under 58.1-802, normally paid by the seller. If your Charlottesville house needs work or has back tax, Cash Home Buyers can review it as is and plan around the payoff figure the Treasurer gives you.

More questions about Charlottesville, VA Property Tax Guide

When are Charlottesville real estate taxes due?

June 5 and December 5, in equal installments. A due date that lands on a weekend moves to the next Monday.

What is the Charlottesville real estate tax rate?

The city lists $0.99 per $100 of assessed value, set by City Council. Confirm the current rate with the Treasurer, since council sets it each spring.

How do I dispute my Charlottesville assessment?

Call the City Assessor at 434-970-3136, then file an Assessment Appeal Application. If you disagree with the decision, ask the Board of Equalization to review it within 30 days, and use Circuit Court as the final step.

What happens if Charlottesville property tax goes unpaid?

A 10 percent penalty applies the day after the deadline, and interest accrues at 10 percent a year. The city lists liens and wage garnishment, and judicial sale for three or more years of unpaid tax.

Can I sell a Charlottesville house with tax still due?

Yes, the balance is normally paid from proceeds at closing. Get a current payoff from the Treasurer's Office before the closing date.
